Question B-006-011-008.

Why the correct answer is right: Front-to-back ratio compares power radiated in the antenna's forward direction with power radiated in the opposite, back direction. It is a directional pattern ratio.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "The ratio of the power radiated by the director element, to the power radiated by the reflector element": Yagi elements are not evaluated by separately measuring director power against reflector power; the ratio refers to the whole antenna pattern forward and backward.
- sourceIndex 2: "The ratio of the length of the director element, to the length of the reflector element": Element lengths help create the pattern, but front-to-back ratio is measured in radiated power directions, not physical length ratio.
- sourceIndex 3: "The ratio of the driven element-to-director spacing, to the driven element-to-reflector spacing": Spacing is a design variable. The front-to-back result is the forward lobe power compared with the rear lobe power.
